headline: Maui Police Commission Meeting October 1, 2021

meeting.summary: The chair said the interviews would be held in open session unless private matters came up.
meeting.recap: The chair said the interviews would be held in open session unless private matters came up.[[0:05:22]] Each candidate answered the same 15 questions, with up to five minutes per answer.[[0:06:40]] One question said the police department's budget is about $63 million, with 12.8 percent spent on overtime.[[1:03:10]] Candidates were asked what they would do about a made-up unwritten policy that gives special treatment to off-duty officers, elected officials and officers' families.[[1:52:00]] Candidates were asked how police should respond to Maui's homeless population.[[2:23:52]] Candidates were asked how they would balance openness and secrecy and speed up posting the department's general orders (written rules) on its website.[[2:54:20]] The last question asked whether a background check, the next step if a candidate is offered the job, would show any past problems.[[3:40:00]] The chair said this completed the interviews of the final candidates.[[3:50:53]]
meeting.next: If the commission offers a candidate the chief position, the next step is an extensive background check.

moments.q: Interviews begin with the first question
